title: Tailings transfer pump, casing wear-through
tests: Natural deterioration; physical-only root; no spare, standby out; weak actions with no interval.
summary: The volute liner on tailings pump P-4120 wore through after 4,100 h, in line with the last four sets. Standby P-4121 was already down waiting on an impeller. The plant ran on a bypass for 3 days. The tree stops at 'liner reached end of life', natural vs forced is undecided, and the only preventive action is 'change liner on a planned basis' with no interval.

problem.title: Volute liner wear-through on tailings pump P-4120
problem.site: Iron ore beneficiation plant, Pilbara WA
problem.whatHappened: The volute liner of P-4120 wore through at the cutwater on 9 May 2026 and slurry sprayed from the casing split. The pump tripped on low discharge pressure after 4,100 hours on this liner. Standby P-4121 was out of service with its impeller removed, so the plant ran on a bypass at reduced tails rate for 3 days until a liner arrived.
problem.where: Cutwater area of the volute liner on P-4120.
problem.when: Pump in normal duty on VSD. Noticed rougher sound for about a week before the trip.
problem.impact: Plant at about 60% feed for 72 hours, about 30 hours of lost production. Slurry spray onto the pad, clean-up by vacuum truck. No injury.
problem.makeModel: Hard-metal lined 6/4 slurry pump, 90 kW VSD
problem.duty: Tailings transfer from thickener to storage facility, duty/standby

evidence.title: Run hours and liner change history, last four sets
evidence.note: Liner lives 4,600, 4,450, 4,300 and 4,100 h. Current set ran 4,100 h.

evidence.title: Wear-through at the cutwater
evidence.note: Hole about 40 mm at the cutwater. Even wear pattern, no gouging or cavitation pitting seen. Liner hardness not measured.

evidence.title: Tailings density and sizing log
evidence.note: Density 1.38 to 1.42 t/m3 steady across the period. Sieve P80 about 150 microns, same as last year.

evidence.title: Work order for standby P-4121
evidence.note: WO raised 22 Apr for impeller wear. Part on order, 6 week lead time. Still open on 9 May.

evidence.title: Store stock list
evidence.note: No spare volute liner for the 6/4 pump on hand. One impeller on hand. No min/max set for liners.

evidence.title: Operator
evidence.note: Pump sounded rougher for about a week. Not logged. No casing thickness checks are done on any slurry pump.

mustSuggest.idea: No wear monitoring (casing thickness) or planned change point set from the liner life history
No spare liner held and no min/max, so the repair waited 49 days lead time
Rough sound was noticed but there is no way or expectation to log it
Wear rate is normal for this abrasive duty (lives 4,100 to 4,600 h) or abnormal, with a way to check

acceptable: Standby availability not managed (standby down 17 days)
Liner material suitability for the duty as a question, not a conclusion
Pump speed on the VSD relative to best efficiency flow
wrongOrDangerous: Operator should have reported the noise sooner (blame)
Cavitation or misalignment stated as the cause with no evidence
Forced deterioration declared, because the lives are consistent

mustFlag.note: Flagged root is only the liner end of life
Wear is natural or forced, never decided
Only a vague preventive action exists

mustNotFlag: missing_level without noting n5 is a system cause already in the tree
challenge.expectation: Summary says the analysis stops at the wear and that the system side (monitoring, spares, standby) needs to be carried through.
deliberateWeaknesses: Flagged root cause n2 is physical only, with no human or system cause beneath it (stopped_at_physical)
n1 and n2: natural vs forced not decided (deterioration_undecided)
Only preventive action a3 has no interval, no craft, no owner (no_task_interval, action_weak)
n5 (the real system gap) is not flagged as a root cause

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Liner lives of 4,100 to 4,600 h are consistent and the slurry density and sizing are unchanged. This looks like normal wear that is managed, not removed.
corrective: Replace liner (a1 done) and repair standby (a2): do not repeat

preventive.what: Ultrasonic thickness readings on the volute at the cutwater and discharge against a minimum thickness
Planned liner change set from the history, shorter than the shortest recent life (4,100 h)
preventive.interval: starting point about 3,500 h run, to check against site history and OEM guidance

preventive.what: Hold a volute liner and an impeller for the 6/4 pump with a min/max in stores
Standby pump out of service for more than a set time triggers a priority review
Log an unusual sound or vibration on the round sheet

capa.spares: Volute liner and impeller for the 6/4 pump; reason is the 49 day lead time and the standby already down.
capa.rollout: All pumps of the same size and duty on tailings and thickener underflow: add thickness readings and check liner stock.
unacceptable: Find and remove the forcing cause as the main action (wrong for natural)
Inventing a material grade or price
